title: Germany Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte) 2027: Points, Costs and Strategy
seoTitle: Chancenkarte 2027: Germany Opportunity Card Points System
seoDescription: The Chancenkarte lets graduates live in Germany for 12 months job-hunting with 20-hour work rights. Full points table, blocked account amounts and strategy for 2027.
intro: Germany’s points-based Opportunity Card grants a 12-month job-seeking stay with part-time work rights. The full points table and a working strategy.
description: Chancenkarte 2027: eligibility gates, the 6-point threshold, funds requirement and how to use the card.
author: NextApply Team
excerpt: The Chancenkarte’s full points table, funds requirement and a working 12-month strategy.
content:
Germany’s Opportunity Card — Chancenkarte — is a points-based job-seeker visa that lets you move to Germany for up to a year without an employment contract, hunt for qualified work on the ground, and take trial jobs with employers while you search. Since its June 2024 launch it has quietly become the practical back door into the German labour market for graduates who do not yet have a PhD offer or a signed contract. The rules are precise, and the points table decides everything.

The two gates you must pass first

Before points even count, two basic criteria are non-negotiable: a recognised university degree or at least two years of state-recognised vocational training, and either German at A1 or English at B2. You must also show you can fund yourself — a blocked account with roughly €1,000-1,100 per month for the year (the exact job-seeker rate is updated annually), or a part-time job offer. Recognition of your qualification is checked through the official ANABIN database and the ZAB statement of comparability — start that process months before applying, because it is the slowest document in the file.

The points table

You need 6 of a possible 14 points. The current allocation:

[[chart:chancenkarte-points]]
CriterionPoints
Recognised degree or vocational training of at least two years4 (partial recognition: 3)
German A2 / B11 / 2 (extra point if both German and English)
English C11
At least 2 years of work experience in the last 5 years2
At least 5 years of work experience in the last 7 years3
Age 35 or younger2
Age 36-401
Previous stay in Germany (6 months in recent years)1
Spouse eligible for the Opportunity Card too1

Most degree-holders clear the threshold with age plus experience plus language — a 28-year-old with an English B2 certificate, two years of work and a recognised degree banks 4+2+2 = 8 points without speaking a word of German. But the card is also designed to reward exactly what German employers say they lack: German language, trade experience and youth.

What the card lets you do

The Chancenkarte grants a 12-month stay for job-seeking, with part-time work up to 20 hours a week and unlimited two-week trial employments — an unusual right that turns interviews into paid auditions. Once you sign a qualified contract, you switch to a skilled-worker or EU Blue Card residence permit, and the clock towards permanent settlement continues from there. The card does not extend for a second year of searching, so treat the twelve months as a campaign: prepare German to A2-B1 before arrival, target shortage occupations (IT, engineering, healthcare, crafts), and use the trial-work right aggressively.

The document file, assembled once

Chancenkarte applications fail on documents more than on points. The core file: a passport valid well beyond the year, the ZAB statement of comparability (or ANABIN-printed recognition evidence) for your degree, language certificates — Goethe/.telc for German, IELTS/TOEFL for English — proof of funds through the blocked account or a part-time offer, health insurance valid from arrival, and a CV in German tabular format. Vocational applicants add their training certificates and, where relevant, a licence to practise. Everything non-German needs certified translation; everything apostilled from home arrives stronger than originals.

Rejections cluster around three avoidable causes: qualifications not recognised because ANABIN shows only partial equivalence and no ZAB statement was obtained; funds proven but insurance missing; and language claimed at B2 without a certificate — self-assessed English does not count. Each has a bureaucratic fix that takes weeks, not days, which is why the file belongs in motion two to three months before your intended departure.

How researchers and students use it

For our readers the card fills a specific gap: the graduate who finished a master’s abroad, has no German offer, and wants to convert German research-group interviews from Zoom to in-person. With a degree and English B2, most young graduates reach six points easily; German lessons push the file into comfortable territory. The blocked-account mechanics are identical to the student version — our blocked account guide walks through opening, deposits and payouts.

Apply at the German mission in your country; processing typically runs four to twelve weeks. The card is free of agent fees by design — the federal portal and consulates publish everything officially, and anyone selling "guaranteed Chancenkarte" services is selling air.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many points do I need for the Opportunity Card?

You need at least six points on the Chancenkarte points table, alongside a recognised degree or completed vocational training, German at A1 or English at B2, and proof of funds (currently a blocked account of roughly €1,027 per month of the intended stay or €12,324 for a year). Points come from qualifications, language levels, age, German connections and work experience, with a partial-equivalence degree adding a decisive four points.

Can the Chancenkarte lead to permanent residence?

Yes, and that is its core design. You get 12 months to find qualified employment (extendable to 24 with proven progress), during which you can work 20 hours a week and run trial employment. Once you convert into a skilled-worker Blue Card or employment permit, your Chancenkarte months count toward the residence time required for Niederlassungserlaubnis.

Is the Chancenkarte better than a job seeker visa?

It replaces and improves the old job seeker route: you may work part-time while searching, and the points system admits people who do not hold a fully recognised degree yet. The trade-off is the financial proof and the 12-month clock. If you already hold a concrete job offer, skip the Chancenkarte and apply directly for the EU Blue Card or a skilled-worker permit.
